title: Stationary Ergodic Sources and Universal Coding

items.title: Finite-alphabet stationary source
items.statement:
Consider a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal A$, a probability measure $P$ on $\mathcal A^{\mathbb Z}$, and the left shift $T(x)_j=x_{j+1}$.

The shift is measurable on the product sigma-algebra. Call $P$ stationary when it is measure preserving under this shift, precisely the condition in [[def-measure-preserving-transformation-and-system]].

For a stationary $P$, call the source ergodic when each event $E$ satisfying $T^{-1}E=E$ has $P(E)\in\{0,1\}$; by [[def-ergodic-measure-preserving-system]] this is exactly ergodicity of the probability system.
items.strategy: Define the path space, coordinate process, canonical shift, stationarity and ergodicity; state the finite-alphabet and two-sided conventions.

items.title: Finite-block information and entropy in bits
items.statement:
Consider a finite alphabet $\mathcal A$ and a random block $X_0^{n-1}$ with law $p_n$ on $\mathcal A^n$.

Define $\log_2t:=\ln t/\ln2$ for $t>0$. The denominator is positive because $2>1$, $\ln$ is strictly increasing, and $\ln1=0$ by [[def-natural-logarithm]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]. For every positive-probability block $x$, define its information in bits by $I_n^{(2)}(x)=-\log_2p_n(x)$; values on zero-probability blocks may be set to $+\infty$ because they are never sampled.

Define block entropy in bits by
$H_n^{(2)}:=\mathbb E I_n^{(2)}(X_0^{n-1})=H_{\rm nat}(p_n)/\ln2.$
Finite summation and [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]] show this equals $-\sum_{x:p_n(x)>0}p_n(x)\log_2p_n(x)$. Thus the library's entropy interface stays in nats while this page's information and coding rates use bits. For finite-valued $U,V$, also define conditional entropy by $H_2(U\mid V)=\sum_{v:P(V=v)>0}P(V=v)H_2(P_{U\mid V=v})$; zero-probability conditioning values are omitted.
items.strategy: Use the finite probability entropy definition and convert natural units to bits by division by ln 2.

items.title: Binary prefix codes on finite supports
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a finite nonempty message set. A **binary prefix code on $M$** is an injective assignment $c:M\to\{0,1\}^*$ such that no assigned string is a proper initial segment of another assigned string. Write $\ell(m):=|c(m)|$ for its codeword lengths. For a probability vector $p$ on $M$, its expected length is
$$L_p(c):=\sum_{m\in M}p(m)\ell(m).$$

The empty string is permitted only when $M$ is a singleton. In that case it describes one known source block, or a known number of copies of the sole message; the message count is part of the framing convention. For arbitrary concatenations whose message count is not supplied, require every codeword to be nonempty. Thus a singleton source can retain a zero-bit code for one known block without claiming unknown-count decoding.
items.strategy: State the support-only convention; zero-probability source outcomes need not be encoded.

items.title: Triangular averages of finite-past information converge to the infinite-past average
items.statement: If nonnegative integrable-envelope functions g_k converge almost surely to g, proves the triangular averages of (g_k-g) circ T^k tend to zero almost surely and in L1 on a finite measure-preserving system.
items.strategy: Bound tails by the decreasing integrable envelopes Delta_m; apply Birkhoff and its L1 convergence on each Delta_m, then let m increase.

items.title: Finite KL nonnegativity for subprobability references
items.statement: Proves $\ln t\le t-1$ for $t>0$ and, for finite probability weights $p$ and positive-on-support reference weights $q$ with $\sum_iq_i\le1$, proves $\sum_{i:p_i>0}p_i\log_2(p_i/q_i)\ge0$ by an explicit finite argument without choice.
items.strategy: Bound the integral logarithm on both sides of one, then sum the inequality against the probability weights and use the subprobability bound.

items.title: Finite-block LZ78 incremental prefix code
items.statement:
**Input:** A finite alphabet $\mathcal A$ of size $q\ge2$, a finite word $x_0^{n-1}\in\mathcal A^n$, and a terminator $\#$ not in $\mathcal A$. Fix an injective $s_q:=\lceil\log_2(q+1)\rceil$-bit symbol field for $\mathcal A\cup\{\#\}$. The alphabet convention is that of [[def-finite-alphabet-stationary-source]]. The output is a terminated binary record stream; prefix codes use [[def-finite-support-binary-prefix-code]].

1. Start with dictionary $D[0]=\epsilon$ and unread text $x_0^{n-1}\#$. While text remains, let $w$ be the longest dictionary word prefixing the unread text, let $i$ be its dictionary index, and let $c$ be the next symbol. Output the record $(i,c)$ and remove the prefix $wc$ from the unread text. If $c\ne\#$, append $wc$ as the next dictionary entry; if $c=\#$, stop without inserting the terminal phrase.

2. Serialize each parent index $i\ge0$ by the Elias-delta code of $m=i+1$. Put $b=\lfloor\log_2m\rfloor+1$ and $d=\lfloor\log_2b\rfloor+1$. Emit $d-1$ zeros, then the $d$-bit binary expansion of $b$, then the final $b-1$ bits of the $b$-bit binary expansion of $m$. Append the fixed-width symbol field for $c$. Concatenate these records in parser order, including the final marker record.

3. To decode an encoded block, start with dictionary $D[0]=\epsilon$. Read zeros until the first $1$ of an index header; if there are $d-1$ zeros, read that $1$ and the following $d-1$ bits as $b$. Read the next $b-1$ bits and prepend $1$ to recover $m$; put $i=m-1$. Read the next $s_q$ bits as $c$, and emit $D[i]c$. Append that phrase to the dictionary when $c\ne\#$, then read the next record. At the first $c=\#$, stop without insertion and remove the terminal marker from the decoded text. The decoder is specified on valid encoded streams and is not supplied the source length or record count.

Ordinary inserted phrases are dictionary entries; the final phrase containing $\#$ is an output record but is not a dictionary entry. Losslessness, the prefix property and the exact index-length bound are proved in [[thm-lz78-prefix-code-lossless]].
items.strategy: Specify all parsing, dictionary update, encoding, decoding, block reset and termination steps; distinguish this exact code from implementation-specific variants.

items.title: Asymptotically mean stationary sources
items.statement:
Consider a probability law $P$ on $\mathcal A^{\mathbb Z}$ and the left shift $T$.

The law $P$ is asymptotically mean stationary (AMS) when for every measurable event $E$ the limit
$\bar P(E)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}P(T^{-j}E)$
exists and the resulting set function is a probability measure.

The resulting law $\bar P$ is called the stationary mean when it is stationary in the sense of [[def-finite-alphabet-stationary-source]]. If $E$ is strictly shift invariant, then each summand $P(T^{-j}E)=P(E)$; hence $P(E)=\bar P(E)$. Tail events are handled by the separate domination lemma, not by this invariant-event identity.

Call the AMS source ergodic when its stationary mean $\bar P$ is ergodic as a measure-preserving system under the same shift. This is a property of the mean, not a claim that $P$ itself is stationary.
items.strategy: Specify the two-sided path convention, shift direction, setwise cylinder convergence and stationary-mean convention.

items.title: Fixed-length lossless block codes and error probability
items.statement:
Consider a finite alphabet $\mathcal A$, a positive integer $n$, and a decoder output set.

A fixed-length lossless block code of rate $R$ bits per symbol is an injective map from $\mathcal A^n$ into a message set of size at most $2^{\lfloor nR\rfloor}$; the decoder is its inverse on the image.

A code with block error is a pair of encoder and decoder maps whose success set is the set of source blocks decoded correctly; its error probability is the law of the complement of that set. The codebook cardinality bounds the size of the success set by the number of messages.
items.strategy: State encoder, decoder, success set, block-error convention and rate explicitly.

items.title: Finite-state compressibility of an individual sequence
items.statement:
Consider a finite alphabet $\mathcal A$ and a one-sided infinite sequence $x=x_0x_1\cdots$.

An information-lossless $s$-state encoder consists of a finite state set $S$, an initial state, an update map $g:S\times\mathcal A\to S$, and an output map $f:S\times\mathcal A\to\{0,1\}^*$. It is information-lossless when for each initial state the map from finite input words to (concatenated output, final state) is injective.

Let $L_E(x_0^{n-1})$ be its concatenated output length and set $\rho_s(x)=\inf_E\limsup_nL_E(x_0^{n-1})/n$, over information-lossless encoders with at most $s$ states. Define finite-state compressibility $\rho_{\rm FS}(x)=\inf_{s\ge1}\rho_s(x)$. The infima are nonincreasing in $s$ and bounded below by zero, so the limit in the equivalent notation $\lim_{s\to\infty}\rho_s(x)$ exists.
items.strategy: Specify encoder states, transitions, output strings, information-losslessness and the limsup/inf conventions; normalize by log2 of the source alphabet size.

items.title: Information rate of a general finite-alphabet process
items.statement:
Consider a finite alphabet $\mathcal A$ and a process law $P$ on $\mathcal A^{\mathbb N_0}$; $H_n:=H(X_0^{n-1})$ is as in [[def-finite-block-information-and-entropy]].

Define the upper information rate $\overline h(P):=\limsup_{n\to\infty}H_n/n$ and, when the limsup and liminf agree, the information rate $h(P):=\lim_{n\to\infty}H_n/n$. This definition does not assume stationarity.

Since $X_0^{n-1}$ has at most $|\mathcal A|^n$ values, $0\le H_n\le n\log_2|\mathcal A|$; consequently both rates are defined and lie in $[0,\log_2|\mathcal A|]$.
items.strategy: State the block-entropy convention and limsup definition for a process that need not be stationary.

items.title: LZ77 previous-match length and recurrence time
items.statement:
Consider a finite alphabet $\mathcal A$ and a two-sided sequence $x\in\mathcal A^{\mathbb Z}$.

For positive integers $n,W$, define the backward recurrence time of the current length-$n$ block by
$R_n(x)=\inf\{j\ge1:(x_{-j},\ldots,x_{-j+n-1})=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})\},$
with $R_n=+\infty$ if the set is empty. The start offset is positive, so the current block is not counted as its own match.

Define its previous-match phrase length in a window of width $W$ by
$L_W(x)=\max\{n\ge0:R_n(x)\le W\},$
where the empty match of length zero is always allowed. For a periodic sequence, $L_W$ can be infinite; the recurrence-time theorem will only be used to infer the logarithmic inverse relation in probability when $h>0$.
items.strategy: Define R_l and L_n on two-sided finite-alphabet paths and state the equivalence of the events {R_l>n} and {L_n<l} under the selected indexing convention.

items.title: Finite-past information densities
items.statement:
Consider a stationary finite-alphabet source $(X_i)_{i\in\mathbb Z}$ with law $P$ and alphabet $\mathcal A$.

For $k\ge0$, let $\mathcal F_k=\sigma(X_{-k},\ldots,X_{-1})$, with $\mathcal F_0$ trivial. For each $a\in\mathcal A$, define $p_k(a)=P(X_0=a\mid\mathcal F_k)$ by averaging over the finite atoms of $\mathcal F_k$, and put $g_k=-\log_2p_k(X_0)$ on the event $p_k(X_0)>0$, with arbitrary value on its null complement.

The selected probability is positive almost surely: on each atom $B\in\mathcal F_k$ with $P(B)>0$, $P(X_0=a\mid B)=0$ implies $P(B\cap\{X_0=a\})=0$. Thus $g_k$ is finite almost surely; [[def-finite-alphabet-stationary-source]] identifies the same distributions after shifting any finite window.
items.strategy: Specify the conditional-probability convention on positive-probability atoms and the zero-probability null-set convention.

items.title: Entropy lower and Shannon upper bounds for finite prefix codes
items.statement: For a finite distribution, proves every binary prefix code has expected length at least H and constructs a prefix code with expected length less than H+1 bit.
items.strategy: Use Kraft and nonnegative relative entropy for the lower bound; request lengths ceil(-log2 p(x)) and finite Kraft allocation for the upper bound.

items.title: Finite entropy chain rule and monotonicity under conditioning
items.statement: Proves the finite-alphabet entropy chain rule and that conditioning on additional finite-valued variables cannot increase conditional entropy, in bits.
items.strategy: Expand the finite sums for the chain rule; use concavity of Shannon entropy on each conditioning fiber for monotonicity.

items.title: AEP criterion for fixed-rate lossless coding
items.statement: For any finite-alphabet source with -n^{-1}log2 P(X^n) converging in probability to h, proves vanishing block error is achievable for R>h and impossible for R<h.
items.strategy: Use the high-probability information typical set for achievability and cardinality of a fixed-rate code for the converse.

items.title: Distinct-phrase count and Ziv inequality
items.statement: For any distinct finite parsing over a finite alphabet and any order-k Markov kernel, proves the finite-block likelihood inequality grouped by phrase length and preceding context.
items.strategy: Group distinct phrases by length and k-context; apply concavity of log and the unit-mass bound for distinct words; bound phrase-count overhead by the entropy of phrase length and context.

items.title: The stationary mean asymptotically dominates an AMS law
items.statement: For an AMS law P with stationary mean Pbar, proves P(T^{-n}G) tends to zero for every event G with Pbar(G)=0.
items.strategy: The mean and AMS law agree on invariant events. The limsup of shifts of a stationary-mean-null event is invariant and null; Fatou then gives vanishing shifted probabilities.

items.title: Losslessness and prefix property of the explicit LZ78 code
items.statement: Proves the specified finite-block LZ78 record stream is prefix-free and decodes the original block exactly, including the explicit terminal symbol.
items.strategy: Use the self-delimiting parent index, fixed-width symbol field, deterministic dictionary recursion, and terminal symbol to show unique parsing and prefix-freeness.

items.title: Entropy-rate limit for a stationary finite-alphabet source
items.statement: Proves that n^{-1}H(X_0,...,X_{n-1}) converges under stationarity and equals the limit of the finite-past conditional entropies.
items.strategy: Apply the chain rule, stationarity and monotonicity of conditional entropies; identify the limit by Cesaro averaging and subadditivity.

items.title: A null future-tail event under the stationary mean is null under the AMS law
items.statement: Assume AC. If the stationary mean asymptotically dominates P, proves every future-tail event E with Pbar(E)=0 satisfies P(E)=0.
items.strategy: Apply countably many Lebesgue decompositions to shifted P; asymptotic domination makes their singular masses vanish uniformly. Represent E as every n-step preimage and use stationarity.

items.title: LZ78 finite-state optimality for individual sequences
items.statement: For each individual infinite sequence over an alphabet of size at least two, the limsup bit rate of the explicit block-reset LZ78 code is at most its finite-state compressibility.
items.strategy: Count distinct complete phrases, lower-bound every information-lossless finite-state encoder by the entropy of its (start state, output word, end state) phrase records, and compare with the explicit LZ78 index overhead.

items.title: Convergence and integrable envelope for finite-past information
items.statement: Proves p_k(a) converges almost surely for each symbol, g_k converges on realized paths, and sup_k g_k is integrable with an explicit exponential tail bound.
items.strategy: The p_k(a) are bounded finite-partition martingales; prove their convergence by a finite upcrossing argument and bound information tails by stopping at the first small conditional probability.

items.title: Expected lossless prefix-code rate for stationary sources
items.statement: For every stationary finite-alphabet source, the optimal expected prefix-code length for X^n divided by n converges to the entropy rate.
items.strategy: Apply the finite-block entropy lower and upper bounds and the stationary entropy-rate limit.

items.title: Componentwise Shannon–McMillan–Breiman theorem
items.statement: For every stationary finite-alphabet source, proves -n^{-1}log_2 P(X_0^{n-1}) converges almost surely and in L1 to the invariant Birkhoff limit of infinite-past information density, with mean equal to the entropy rate in bits.
items.strategy: Factor block probabilities by the chain rule, use the triangular-average lemma, then apply Birkhoff and the stationary entropy-rate theorem.

items.title: LZ78 expected-rate universality for stationary sources
items.statement: For every stationary finite-alphabet source, the expected explicit terminated LZ78 code length per source symbol converges to the entropy rate in bits, without an ergodicity assumption.
items.strategy: The deterministic Ziv inequality gives an upper bound by every finite-order Markov cross-entropy; let memory grow. The prefix-code entropy lower bound gives the converse.

items.title: Conditional block information rate given the infinite past
items.statement: For each $n\ge1$, constructs the conditional law of $X_0^{n-1}$ given the full infinite past by finite-past martingale limits, then proves its realized information per symbol converges almost surely to the entropy rate for every stationary ergodic finite-alphabet source, without choice.
items.strategy: Construct the conditional block law by bounded finite-partition martingales, factor its realized likelihood into one-symbol past probabilities, and apply the ergodic theorem.

items.title: Ergodic Shannon–McMillan–Breiman theorem
items.statement: For a stationary ergodic finite-alphabet source, the componentwise information-rate limit is the constant entropy rate.
items.strategy: The Birkhoff limit is invariant, hence constant under ergodicity; its expectation, already identified with the entropy rate, determines that constant.

items.title: Invariant conditional-entropy description of the SMB limit
items.statement: Under AC, identifies the componentwise SMB limit with E[g_infinity|I], conditional expectation of infinite-past information given the invariant sigma-algebra.
items.strategy: Apply the finite-measure Birkhoff-limit identification to the stationary observable g_infinity circ T^n; isolate AC as the exact dependency of this identification branch.

items.title: Fixed-rate source coding theorem for stationary ergodic sources
items.statement: For a stationary ergodic finite-alphabet source, fixed-rate lossless coding has vanishing block error above the entropy rate and success probability tending to zero below it.
items.strategy: Apply the AEP coding criterion to the ergodic SMB theorem.

items.title: Shannon–McMillan limit for finite-alphabet AMS ergodic sources
items.statement: Assume AC. For a finite-alphabet AMS source whose stationary mean is ergodic with bit entropy rate h, the normalized self-information -n^{-1}log_2 P(X_0^{n-1}) converges P-almost surely to h.
items.strategy: Use bounded finite-future martingales to make prefix boundary terms negligible along a slow diagonal, transfer the stationary-mean SMB limit on tail events, and sandwich the two finite-block likelihood ratios by Markov and Borel–Cantelli.

items.title: Stationary-ergodic LZ77 phrase-length theorem
items.statement: For a stationary ergodic finite-alphabet source with bit entropy rate $h$, define $R_n=\min\{j\ge1:X_{-j}^{-j+n-1}=X_0^{n-1}\}$ using [[def-lz77-previous-match-phrase-length]]. Then $n^{-1}\log_2R_n\to h$ in probability. If $h>0$, the inverse window length satisfies $L_W/\log_2W\to1/h$ in probability as integer $W\to\infty$.
items.strategy: Use Kac return-time integrals to bound the upper tail, count at most one candidate block per offset under the infinite-past conditional law for the lower tail, then invert the monotone recurrence distances.

items.title: Fixed-rate lossless coding for AMS ergodic sources
items.statement: Assume AC. For a finite-alphabet AMS source with ergodic stationary mean, fixed-rate lossless coding has vanishing block error above the stationary-mean entropy rate and success probability tending to zero below it.
items.strategy: Apply the AEP coding criterion to the AMS information limit.

title: Stationary Ergodic Sources and Universal Coding — Examples

items.title: A nonstationary independent source with no entropy-rate limit
items.statement: Constructs independent binary coordinates whose block entropy per symbol has subsequences tending to zero and one by alternating super-exponentially long deterministic and fair-coin blocks.
items.strategy: Compute H(X_0^{n-1}) as the sum of coordinate entropies and compare at the ends of alternating blocks.

items.title: LZ78 parsing of a finite binary word
items.statement: Traces the specified parser and decoder on 0100101001 followed by the explicit terminal symbol, including dictionary indices and exact record sequence.
items.strategy: Apply the algorithm instruction by instruction; display the dictionary trie with every node and edge convention explained.

items.title: IID and two-state Markov entropy rates
items.statement: Computes h=1 bit/symbol for fair IID bits and h=H2(1/4) for the stationary symmetric two-state Markov source with switch probability 1/4; compares the stationary LZ78 expected rates.
items.strategy: Compute block entropies from the exact finite-dimensional laws and apply the stationary entropy-rate and LZ78 universality theorems.
